subject: High-priority: Meridian production latency & error spike — executive alignment and remediation
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@meridianhealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:14:28 -0700
Subject: Production: latency spike and 5xx errors impacting claims ingestion

Ben —

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency this morning around 08:30 PT and a surge of 5xx errors from the Redwood API. Our claims ingestion pipeline is backing up; throughput is down roughly 40% vs baseline and error rate spiked to ~6%. This is affecting downstream SLA windows for claims processing.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Model: redwood-open-30b (pinned)
- First observed: 08:31 PT
- Recent samples attached as prod-ops-dump-20270305.zip (logs + traces)

Can we get an immediate engineering/exec bridge? This is high impact — Meridian execs are asking for a status update and timeline.

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Senior SRE, Meridian Health
alex.gomez@meridianhealth.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:28:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: latency spike and 5xx errors impacting claims ingestion

Alex — thanks for the alert and the log bundle. I’ve pulled the team into a short bridge (details below) and we’ll triage immediately.

Short plan for the next 30/60/120 minutes:
- 0–15m: Confirm root symptom (latency vs. model OOM vs. infra throttling) — Marissa (on-call) leading.
- 15–60m: Apply mitigations: temporary routing to a smaller model variant, increase concurrency ceiling for Meridian Dedicated pool, and flush prefix cache if KV cache shows corruption — Rishi to approve capacity bump.
- 60–120m: Stabilize traffic, validate p99 latency and error rate below SLA, prepare executive summary and customer-facing note.

We’ll also prepare an exec note that outlines potential credit options and next steps. I’ve attached the prod dump you sent to our internal bridge.

Bridge: 09:45 PT (Zoom) — dial-in on the Meridian shared bridge; Redwood execs will join.

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: prod-ops-dump-20270305.zip (logs/traces summary)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:35:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: latency spike and 5xx errors impacting claims ingestion

Ben / team — quick findings from initial triage (0–10m):
- Telemetry shows elevated KV cache miss and lock contention on the model host group serving Meridian’s traffic (shared pool).
- Model inference times increased with long tail at p99; memory usage on two nodes spiked close to thresholds coincident with traffic burst.
- No obvious model OOMs in the logs; we’re seeing repeated token-generation retries that correlate with the 5xx spikes.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (we can stage these during the bridge):
1) Fail over Meridian to redwood-open-7b-tempered for the next 1–2 hours to reduce per-token latency (can be applied at routing layer).
2) Increase the Dedicated pool concurrency by +30% for Meridian (temporary override) and warm additional GPUs.
3) Clear prefix caches for the impacted route to eliminate any corrupted KV state.

I’m preparing a canary config yaml to apply (canary-config-v1.yaml) and will run a targeted traffic switch once Rishi signs off on temporary capacity.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Incident Lead, Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary-config-v1.yaml

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:47:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: latency spike and 5xx errors impacting claims ingestion

Team — I authorize a temporary capacity reservation for Meridian (up to 2 nodes, estimate ~$2.4k/hour) to avoid throttling while we stabilize. Please get a quick approval from finance for emergency spend; I’ll loop in Product for formal communication.

Rationale: switching to 7b reduces p99 by ~40% immediately and buys time for deeper kernel-level investigation. If we can get the route to sub-200ms p95 within 45–60m, we should be able to roll traffic back to the pinned model.

Required asks:
- Ben: confirm exec-level note and credit offer (we should propose a good-faith partial credit for the 6+ hours impacted).
- Marissa: execute canary and observe for 30m; escalate if error rate >1.5%.
- Laura: please approve external exec briefing language and sign off on credit terms.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

Reference: JIRA OPS-9876

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 11:02:54 -0700
Subject: Redwood status update and exec briefing for Meridian (09:45 bridge recap)

Alex — thank you again for the logs and for joining the bridge. Quick update and commitments from Redwood:

What we did (09:45–10:45 PT):
- Failed over Meridian traffic to redwood-open-7b-tempered (canary) for immediate latency reduction.
- Increased Dedicated concurrency for Meridian temporary pool (+30%).
- Flushed prefix cache and restarted the two impacted hosts.

Immediate impact observed:
- Throughput: recovered to ~92% of baseline within 20 minutes of the canary switch.
- Error rate: reduced from ~6% to ~0.8% at 10:15 PT and stable in the last 30 minutes.
- p95 latency: down from 820ms to 230ms after mitigation.

Next actions (owner / ETA):
- Full post-mortem and kernel-level investigation (Marissa / 72h).
- Capacity report and cost reconciliation for temporary nodes (Rishi / 24h).
- Customer-facing root cause and remediation note + proposed credit (Ben / 24h).

Commitment: we prepared an exec-level commitment letter outlining remediation steps and a proposed one-week service credit while we complete the PM and fixes. Attached: exec-commitment-letter.pdf.

Proposed bridge cadence: 4pm PT quick sync for a status update; otherwise we’ll send written updates at 12h and 24h.

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: exec-commitment-letter.pdf

Laura — please sign off on the attached commitment letter when you have a moment. I’ve included the impact numbers for Meridian execs.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@meridianhealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-alerts@meridianhealth.com
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 16:42:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood status update and exec briefing for Meridian (09:45 bridge recap)

Ben — thanks for the rapid response and for the clear remediation steps. We accepted the canary and the traffic switch; errors reduced and backlog started clearing at ~13:05 PT. Meridian execs appreciate the proactive credit offer — we’ll review the letter and confirm.

One small note: we saw a brief ~0.5% uptick in token retries during the switch window but it subsided within 10 minutes. Please include that in the post-mortem.

I’ll join the 4pm sync for a quick handoff and to confirm closure if everything remains stable.

Alex
